quotes.text: You have 7 calendar days to submit evidence.
MB WAY invoices and subscriptions only support the `send_invoice` collection method.
Authorize the payment in the MB WAY app within 4 minutes.
MB WAY doesn’t redirect the browser and doesn’t use a return URL.

old_evidence.text: The Mobile Payment element doesn’t support MB WAY.
Stripe’s company name (`Stripe Inc`) is shown on bank statements along with the transaction amount.

findings: November explicitly marks B2C supported and B2B unsupported, instant access, single-use, domestic and cross-border support, and expands the capabilities and product/API matrices. Portuguese customer location, EUR presentment, the same 40 merchant locations and supported settlement-currency qualification are distinct. Manual capture remains unsupported. November additionally lists partial, multi and over-capture and the listed authorization variations as unsupported, and full disputes only (old raw lines 14–109; new raw lines 10–71 and 104–128).

November documents in-app payments as supported, where the current source's unsupported wording is based on the May 7 capture's specifically named Mobile Payment Element. It documents Billing and Invoicing for hosted invoice payment with send_invoice only, including invoices on subscriptions paid individually by customers. Checkout itself remains one-time only, with no setup mode, SetupIntent, setup_future_usage or off-session payments (old raw lines 101–109; new raw lines 104–147). The separate hosted invoice changelog dates that surface to 2026-07-29.dahlia (raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-07-29-hosted-invoice-page-mb-way-support-2026-11-07.md lines 1–21 and 61–70).

November adds the four-minute app authorization deadline and explicitly explains web polling without browser redirect or return URL, with desktop phone approval and mobile app switching. It also expands the descriptor constraint to PaymentIntent, account and Connect settings. May alone explicitly labels the statement text Stripe Inc (old raw lines 111–118 and 163–165; new raw lines 149–177).

November gives original-method refund return and the Dashboard/API Refund status and refund.updated or refund.failed paths. If the Refund fails the amount returns to the merchant's Stripe balance and the customer must be refunded another way. The up-to-365-days-from-completion limit, typical minutes (not guaranteed), full/multiple partial refund support and the ceiling of the original amount remain. Existing dispute hold, evidence and outcome rules were reorganized and the matrix now explicitly marks partial disputes unsupported (old raw lines 135–161; new raw lines 63–102).

Source lines 13–25 accurately identify the May locations, EUR, phone/app flow and thresholds. Add the B2C and settlement qualification, four-minute pending step and no browser redirect while distinguishing international phone numbers from buyer geography (old raw lines 8–22 and 56–115; new raw lines 9–45 and 149–171).

Source lines 27–31 compress dispute/refund timing and lifecycle. Qualify seven calendar days for dispute evidence, typical minutes for refunds, the partial-refund cumulative cap and failed Refund reconciliation. Date the precise Stripe Inc example to May and use the broader no overrides rule for November (old raw lines 135–165; new raw lines 63–102 and 173–177). The Wallets prose/routes and Stripe company and index routes repeat those shortened claims (wiki/concepts/stripe-wallets.md lines 239–253 and 412, wiki/stripe-index.md line 404 and wiki/companies/stripe.md line 601).

Source lines 33–37 present Mobile Payment Element and recurring support as undated blanket rules and omit the existing full-Dashboard vs capability-request distinction. Date the May Mobile Payment Element sentence, add November's broader in-app row and scope Billing/Invoicing to send_invoice, and preserve one-time Checkout and unsupported automatic recurring/off-session behavior. Separate platform support for all charge types from individual connected-account capability active status (old raw lines 101–109 and 167–177; new raw lines 104–147). Link the source back to its Wallets concept while preserving its existing inbound route at line 412.

Table and heading rearrangement, removal of the demo video link, moving enablement and replacing quickstarts with focused links are presentation/navigation. Existing dispute notification/hold, 7-calendar-day evidence and win/loss flow are substantially the same (old raw lines 117–157; new raw lines 86–102 and 179–183).

Retain source line 33's unsupported manual capture claim (old raw lines 48–50, new raw lines 57–61). November explicitly marks partial, multi and over-capture unsupported, so the overview supplies no split-fulfillment capture path. Qualify source lines 27–29 to reflect distinct support for full disputes, unsupported partial disputes, and support for full and partial refunds. The November refund matrix and refund process explain that multiple partial refunds may total up to the original payment (new raw lines 57–78).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mb-way, November describes a single-use Portuguese customer wallet with EUR presentment, domestic and cross-border support, and the same 40 eligible business locations for payments settling in a supported currency. The account matrix marks B2C supported and B2B unsupported. An international number can still be linked to the wallet (old raw lines 8-38 and 56-99; new raw lines 9-45). The customer authorizes a push in the app within four minutes. The web page polls without a browser redirect or return URL. App approval or returning to the web page alone does not prove payment success. The result is immediate when confirmed and the payout schedule is standard (new raw lines 149-171). Enable MB WAY in Dashboard for Stripe front-end products or follow the manual-integration route. A Connect platform can use all charge types, but connected accounts enable through full Dashboard access or a Capabilities API request as applicable. Check mb_way_payments=active in accounts events or API (new raw lines 131-141 and 179-183). Manual capture remains unsupported (old raw lines 48-50 and new raw lines 57-61). Checkout is one-time only, and hosted invoices on send_invoice can be paid individually, including subscription invoices (new raw lines 104-147). source-stripe-mb-way.md reflects the May payment flow, amount limits, refunds and disputes, but its mobile and recurring restrictions need dated UI and collection-method qualifiers and its refund status coverage is incomplete.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mb-way, November adds explicit B2C eligibility, richer authorization/capture and product/API support matrices, a four-minute approval limit, browser polling without return_url, and terminal Refund statuses and events (old raw lines 101-118 and 135-165; new raw lines 20-45, 47-147 and 149-177). The November matrix marks manual, partial, multi and over-capture unsupported. Full disputes are supported and partial disputes are unsupported. Full and partial refunds are supported (new raw lines 57-78). Refunds return to the original method and can be full or partial up to 365 days after completion, with cumulative partials capped at the original payment. Minutes are typical. Check Refund status or refund.updated/refund.failed. A failed refund puts funds back in the Stripe balance and requires another refund method. Disputes retain a seven-calendar-day evidence deadline and held balance pending outcome. Date the May Mobile Payment Element exclusion and Stripe Inc label in source-stripe-mb-way.md and reciprocally qualify the Wallets route. November's in-app row does not define a universal mobile SDK contract. The distinct iOS 26.6.0 PaymentSheet evidence does not establish account eligibility. Hosted Invoice and Subscription support is send_invoice only, with individual authorization and the 2026-07-29.dahlia changelog scope. Checkout subscription/setup modes, automatic recurring payments and off-session reuse remain unsupported. Endive's Stripe.js pending modal is a separate version-qualified client behavior. Table formatting, the removed video reference and the acceptance parent links are presentation and navigation.
